chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
When omissions become numerous upon you, continue in your prayer, for it is on the verge of leaving you; it is only from Satan.

key_terms.سَهْو: Forgetfulness or omission in ritual acts

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they feel overwhelmed by frequent doubts and omissions during prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) addresses the specific fiqh of *sahw* (forgetfulness) and *shakk* (doubt), advising the worshipper to persist in their prayer rather than restarting, as excessive doubt is typically a distraction from Satan (*waswasa*) that will subside. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of maintaining the continuity of worship despite internal uncertainty, distinguishing between minor doubts that do not break the prayer and those that require verification. The advice highlights the psychological aspect of prayer, where the devil exploits the worshipper's focus to induce paralysis through over-analysis.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the omissions are numerous upon you, so continue in your Salāt, for it is on the verge of leaving you. But rather, it is from the Satanla’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn ai-Husayn from Safwan from af-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has sad,
‘If mistakes become many on you then continue in your Salah (prayer), eventually it may leave you alone; it is from Satan.’”
